body: Blob storage has access tiers that trade storage cost against access cost. The hot tier is for frequently accessed data. The cool tier is for infrequently accessed data kept at least 30 days. The cold tier is for infrequently accessed data kept at least 90 days. The archive tier is for rarely accessed data kept at least 180 days, with flexible latency, such as long-term backups. Archive has the lowest storage cost, but also the highest rehydration latency and access cost.
author: claude

body: Azure Storage keeps copies of your data for protection. Locally redundant storage (LRS) keeps three copies in one datacenter. Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) keeps copies across three availability zones in the primary region. Geo-redundant storage (GRS) uses LRS in the primary region, then copies asynchronously to a secondary region, also with LRS. Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS) uses ZRS in the primary region and copies to the secondary region with LRS. Geo options protect against a whole region failing.
author: claude

body: A storage account type decides which services you can use. Standard general-purpose v2 supports blobs, queues, tables and Azure Files, with SMB file shares only. Premium block blobs is for blob storage only. Premium file shares is for Azure Files only, and it is the only type that supports both SMB and NFS file shares. Premium page blobs holds page blobs only. Premium accounts offer LRS and ZRS redundancy, while page blobs offer LRS only.
author: claude

body: Three tools move files to Azure. AzCopy is a command-line utility for copying blobs or files to and from a storage account, and its synchronization works in one direction only: you choose a source and a destination. Azure Storage Explorer is a graphical app for managing files and blobs, and it uses AzCopy in the background. Azure File Sync is installed on a local Windows server and keeps it bi-directionally synced with files in Azure Files.
author: claude

body: Azure has two main migration helpers. Azure Migrate is a hub for assessing and migrating your on-premises datacenter to Azure, with a unified portal and integrated tools. Azure Data Box is a physical migration service for moving large amounts of data quickly, inexpensively and reliably. Microsoft ships you a Data Box storage device, which has up to 80 terabytes of usable space, you fill it with your data, and a regional carrier takes it back to Azure.
